findings.title: Elysium's announced read precompile and core writer predeploy can reach the PoolManager only as a currency or hook that a pool creator names
findings.difference: Kinetiq plans an ArbOS upgrade, about four weeks after the 9 November 2026 launch, that adds a precompile serving HyperCore order books, prices and balances attested by the sequencer, and an ElysiumCoreWriter predeploy that emits order intents and can call the originating contract back with the outcome. Neither address nor interface is published, and getScheduledUpgrade() still returns zeros.
findings.mechanism: The PoolManager calls out only to a currency (transfer in take, balanceOf in sync and settle), to the hook of a pool key, and to the native recipient of take (src/types/Currency.sol:39-87, src/PoolManager.sol:279-297 and 349-364). The day after the upgrade an ordinary account can name either new address as a currency or a hook in its own pool. If the read precompile answers balanceOf with a value that moves between sync and settle, settle books the difference as a payment in that currency, and take of that currency succeeds when the precompile returns no data, because the transfer check accepts an empty return (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). The credit and the debt are both in the precompile currency, so only pools that list it carry them. A callback from the predeploy reaches the PoolManager only if the PoolManager itself sent the intent, which needs one of its three call shapes to match an intent-emitting selector of the predeploy; the interface is unpublished.
findings.impact: None for pools that do not list the new addresses. A pool that lists one of them as a currency could be filled with an unbacked balance of that currency.
findings.preconditions: Elysium governance ships the upgrade; a pool creator lists the new address as a currency or hook and LPs choose that pool.
findings.mitigations: After the upgrade, call both addresses from the PoolManager in the empty, balanceOf and transfer shapes, as cycles 16 to 38 did for the 337 existing ones, and refuse to integrate pools that list them.

cleared.check: Settlement arithmetic against value that arrives outside msg.value (ArbOS deposits, retryable value, fee distribution to the PoolManager address).
cleared.result: Native settle credits msg.value of the settling call only (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354), and sync of address(0) only resets the synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283), so native value that reaches the PoolManager by any other path is never booked as anyone's payment. Token settles use the balance difference since the caller's own sync (src/PoolManager.sol:356-361), which F-137 already covers for bridge deliveries.
